subject: horse
name: Standing Under Saddle
summary: The horse's ability to stand quietly for mounting, dismounting, and stationary pauses under saddle without walking off.
purpose: Essential for rider safety at mounting and calmness throughout every ride.
safety: Reward stillness patiently rather than rushing off immediately after mounting.

introductory.overview: Standing quietly at a mounting block and pausing calmly under saddle in familiar spaces.

components.title: Mounting stillness
components.description: Waiting calmly while the rider mounts and settles before moving forward on request.

introductory.learning: Stands for mounting with occasional shifting, stepping off early, or impatience.
introductory.proficient: Stands quietly beside a mounting block or on flat ground while the rider mounts, settles, and dismounts, waiting calmly until asked to walk on.

intermediate.overview: Standing patiently under saddle in varied settings, group rides, and busy environments.

components.title: Wait in group or trail settings
components.description: Remaining relaxed at halt while other horses move or riders adjust gear.

intermediate.learning: Stands under saddle in group or novel settings with intermittent fidgeting.
intermediate.proficient: Stands calmly and patiently under saddle in varied environments and group settings without pawing, jigging, or walking off.

subject: horse
name: Walk (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to walk willingly under a rider's weight with pure four-beat rhythm, relaxation, and adjustable stride length.
purpose: Builds foundational under-saddle confidence, supple back movement, four-beat purity, and calm responsiveness.
safety: Allow free use of the head and neck to preserve a natural four-beat walk and avoid poll or back tension.

introductory.overview: Walking forward willingly on light requests in a steady, relaxed four-beat rhythm.

components.title: Calm four-beat walk
components.description: Moving forward evenly with a natural head-and-neck nod without jigging, bracing, or stalling.

components.title: Welfare and common issues
components.description: Tension, rushing, or a tight lateral pace often signals rider hand restriction, saddle discomfort, or anxiety rather than disobedience.

introductory.learning: Walks under saddle with occasional tension, jigging, pacing, or reluctance to step forward calmly.
introductory.proficient: Walks forward willingly and calmly under saddle in a regular, relaxed four-beat rhythm without bracing or jigging.

intermediate.overview: Adjusting walk stride length (stretching into free walk and returning to active working walk) while preserving pure four-beat rhythm.

components.title: Free walk and working walk
components.description: Stretching forward and down willingly on a longer rein and shortening smoothly back into an active working walk without breaking into trot or losing beat purity.

intermediate.learning: Lengthens or shortens walk stride with intermittent loss of four-beat purity, hurrying, or tension.
intermediate.proficient: Reliably adjusts between active working walk and relaxed, ground-covering free walk while preserving pure four-beat rhythm and relaxation.

subject: horse
name: Trot (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to carry a rider in a symmetrical two-beat diagonal trot or jog—progressing from steady rhythm to balanced turns and adjustable self-carriage.
purpose: Develops under-saddle balance, two-beat symmetry, muscular stamina, and responsive tempo adjustment across English and Western styles.
safety: Build trot duration gradually according to the horse's fitness and balance; sudden unevenness warrants slowing down to assess soundness or saddle fit.

introductory.overview: Trotting or jogging willingly under saddle in a steady two-beat diagonal rhythm on simple lines and large turns.

components.title: Steady two-beat rhythm
components.description: Maintaining even opposite-side diagonal footfalls without rushing, hollowing, or unexpectedly breaking back to walk; visible suspension is not required in a slow jog or early working trot.

introductory.learning: Trots short stretches with occasional rushing, breaking gait, hollowing, or tension.
introductory.proficient: Trots or jogs willingly under saddle in a steady, relaxed two-beat rhythm on straight lines and large turns without rushing or losing balance.

intermediate.overview: Carrying balanced, adjustable trot tempo through turns, 20 m circles, and transitions with soft responsiveness to light cues.

components.title: Balance on curves and tempo control
components.description: Maintaining two-beat symmetry through corners and circles without falling inward on the shoulder, and responding softly to moderate tempo adjustments on either light contact or a loose rein.

intermediate.learning: Adjusts trot tempo or holds balance through turns with intermittent rushing, leaning, or falling inward.
intermediate.proficient: Trots with consistent rhythm, relaxed back, and adjustable tempo through turns, circles, and progressive transitions in both directions.

advanced.overview: Demonstrating sustained self-carriage, clear within-gait lengthenings and shortenings, and steady cadence through demanding figures and lateral work.

components.title: Self-carriage and stride adjustability
components.description: Lengthening and shortening the trot stride from active hindquarters without quickening into rushing, leaning on the reins, or losing two-beat purity across complex lines and movements.

advanced.learning: Practices within-gait trot lengthenings, shortenings, or demanding figures with intermittent loss of cadence, straightness, or relaxation.
advanced.proficient: Maintains uphill self-carriage, elastic back movement, and pure two-beat rhythm through clear trot lengthenings, shortenings, and demanding figures in both directions without tension.

subject: horse
name: Canter (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's calm comprehension, three-beat rhythm, lead reliability, simple lead changes, and adaptable self-carriage in canter or lope—prioritizing physical comfort and relaxation over speed or specialized maneuvers.
purpose: Builds relaxed three-beat balance, symmetrical lead strength, within-gait adjustability, and willing comfort under saddle.
safety: Ensure adequate space, good footing, and balanced walk or trot preparation before asking a green horse to canter.
Persistent one-sided lead resistance, hollowing, rushing, or frequent cross-cantering can indicate soreness, saddle fit issues, or conditioning gaps—evaluate welfare before increasing demands.

introductory.overview: Departing calmly into canter or lope, maintaining a three-beat rhythm on simple lines and large curves, and returning safely to trot or walk.

components.title: Calm depart and three-beat rhythm
components.description: Cantering forward willingly without bolting, bucking, or disuniting; consistent lead selection on request is not yet required at this level.

introductory.learning: Canters short stretches with occasional rushing, cross-cantering, or abrupt downward breaks.
introductory.proficient: Departs calmly into canter or lope, maintains a relaxed three-beat rhythm for sustained stretches on simple lines/large curves, and returns safely to trot or walk on request.

intermediate.overview: Departing reliably on the requested lead in both directions, holding balance on generous curves, and performing calm simple lead changes.

components.title: Lead reliability and curve balance
components.description: Taking the requested left or right lead calmly from walk or trot and maintaining even three-beat balance through turns without leaning inward or falling onto the forehand.

components.title: Simple lead changes
components.description: Transitioning smoothly through walk or trot to depart calmly onto the new lead without rushing or tension.

intermediate.learning: Takes requested leads and performs simple changes with occasional wrong-lead starts, rushing, or loss of balance on curves.
intermediate.proficient: Reliably departs on the requested lead in both directions, maintains balanced three-beat rhythm on straight lines and 20 m circles, and performs calm, balanced simple lead changes.

advanced.overview: Maintaining adaptable three-beat self-carriage and within-gait stride adjustability (lengthening and shortening smoothly without rushing) across varied curves, terrain, and transitions suited to the horse's build and conditioning. Counter-canter and flying lead changes are tracked separately.

components.title: Within-gait stride adjustability
components.description: Lengthening and shortening the canter or lope stride smoothly from engaged hindquarters while preserving relaxed three-beat rhythm rather than speeding up or pulling flat.

components.title: Adaptable balance and posture
components.description: Carrying balanced, unbraced alignment across varied lines, gentle terrain, and upward or downward transitions in both directions without tension.

advanced.learning: Practices within-gait canter stride adjustments and varied balanced lines with intermittent rushing, flattening onto the forehand, crookedness, or mild brace.
advanced.proficient: Carries comfortable, balanced three-beat self-carriage in both directions—smoothly lengthening and shortening canter stride on light cues without rushing or tension—and adapts rhythm and alignment calmly across varied lines, footing, and transitions suited to its build.

subject: horse
name: Counter-Canter (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's calm comprehension and balanced three-beat carriage when asked to stay on the outside canter lead through straight lines, shallow loops, and curved tracks without swapping early or losing composure.
purpose: Develops symmetrical hindquarter strength, lateral balance, and relaxed responsiveness to rider alignment as an optional extension beyond fundamental lead control.
safety: Build strength gradually on straight lines and wide shallow curves on supportive footing; never force tight counter-canter turns if a horse struggles physically or loses balance.
Repeated cross-cantering, pinned ears, or abrupt swapping on one lead may indicate fatigue, saddle pressure, or stifle/sacroiliac discomfort—assess welfare early.

intermediate.overview: Maintaining calm, balanced counter-canter along straight lines and wide shallow curves in both directions without swapping leads unintentionally or hollowing.

components.title: Relaxed straightness on the outside lead
components.description: Staying steady in three-beat rhythm with slight comfortable alignment toward the leading side rather than bracing or speeding up.

intermediate.learning: Holds counter-canter briefly on shallow curves with occasional unintended lead swaps, rushing, or breaking back to trot.
intermediate.proficient: Calmly maintains balanced three-beat counter-canter along straight lines and shallow curves in both directions on light cues without rushing, hollowing, or swapping leads unintentionally.

advanced.overview: Sustaining poised, adjustable counter-canter through deeper curves, loops, and varied transitions with relaxed self-carriage and comfort.

components.title: Strength and suppleness through deeper turns
components.description: Carrying weight smoothly behind through deeper curved counter-canter lines and responding calmly to stride adjustments.

advanced.learning: Sustains deeper counter-canter loops with intermittent crookedness, hurried tempo, or loss of three-beat balance.
advanced.proficient: Carries poised, balanced, relaxed counter-canter through deeper curves and loops in both directions—maintaining three-beat purity and responsive stride adjustability without tension or unintended swaps.

subject: horse
name: Flying Lead Changes (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's calm comprehension, straightness, and coordinated balance when switching front and hind canter leads simultaneously in the air on light cues.
purpose: Demonstrates advanced symmetrical hind-leg strength, timing clarity, and mental relaxation in an optional specialized maneuver.
safety: Require calm simple lead changes and balanced self-carriage before introducing flying changes; rushing, bucking, kicking out, or chronic late hind changes point to confusion or back/hock discomfort.

advanced.overview: Responding calmly and straight on light cues to change front and hind leads cleanly together during suspension in both directions without rushing, anticipation, or tension.

components.title: Straightness and simultaneous swap
components.description: Stepping cleanly into the new lead behind and in front in the same stride without diving sideways, speeding up afterward, or dragging the hind change late.

components.title: Emotional composure
components.description: Remaining settled before and after the change rather than anticipating or kicking out.

advanced.learning: Performs flying changes with occasional anticipation, rushing afterward, crookedness, late hind changes, or swishing tail/tension.
advanced.proficient: Calmly understands light cues to perform straight, balanced, simultaneous flying lead changes in both directions with relaxed posture and steady rhythm before and after the change—without rushing, kicking out, or defensive tension.

subject: horse
name: Transitions (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's responsiveness to upward, downward, halt, and rebalancing requests under saddle.
purpose: Reflects attentiveness, physical balance, and willingness to shift weight smoothly between gaits.
safety: Give clear, fair preparation before asking for transitions.

introductory.overview: Responding calmly to basic halt, walk, and trot requests without bracing or rushing.

components.title: Basic halt and gait changes
components.description: Stopping calmly on light request and moving off smoothly.

introductory.learning: Responds to basic halt and walk/trot requests with occasional delay or leaning on the bit/halter.
introductory.proficient: Responds calmly and willingly to halt, walk, and trot requests without bracing, tossing the head, or rushing.

intermediate.overview: Prompt, balanced progressive transitions across walk, trot, and canter—plus responding softly to rebalancing (half-halt) requests.

components.title: Rebalancing response
components.description: Checking balance and engaging slightly on a subtle rebalancing cue without breaking gait.

intermediate.learning: Executes progressive transitions and rebalancing checks with intermittent hollowing or falling onto the forehand.
intermediate.proficient: Performs smooth, balanced progressive transitions across all three gaits and responds softly to rebalancing requests while staying relaxed and straight.

advanced.overview: Balanced direct transitions (halt–trot, walk–canter, canter–walk) and within-gait lengthenings/shortenings with uphill self-carriage.

components.title: Direct and within-gait balance
components.description: Shifting weight cleanly onto the hindquarters through demanding gait changes.

advanced.learning: Practices direct or within-gait transitions with occasional loss of straightness or cadence.
advanced.proficient: Executes crisp, uphill direct transitions and within-gait adjustments cleanly in both directions without tension.

subject: horse
name: Steering & Navigation (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to follow straight lines, curves, figures, and marker patterns calmly with appropriate alignment and bend.
purpose: Unifies straightness, bend, and pattern responsiveness under saddle across gaits.
safety: Keep turns wide enough for the horse's balance and footing at the current gait.

introductory.overview: Following straight lines away from the rail, ~20 m circles, turns, and simple marker paths at walk without drifting.

components.title: Walk straightness and turns
components.description: Stepping evenly off the rail and bending softly around gentle walk turns.

introductory.learning: Follows walk lines and circles with occasional drifting toward the gate/rail or stiffening through the ribs.
introductory.proficient: Walks straight lines away from the rail, ~20 m circles, and simple marker patterns calmly on light steering requests without drifting.

intermediate.overview: Maintaining steady rhythm, uniform bend, and clean direction changes through figures and patterns (circles, serpentines, slaloms) at trot.

components.title: Trot bend and balance
components.description: Changing bend smoothly from left to right without speeding up or falling inward.

intermediate.learning: Negotiates trot figures and patterns with intermittent bulging through the shoulder or rushing.
intermediate.proficient: Maintains steady rhythm, soft uniform bend, and smooth changes of direction through trot figures and marker patterns without rushing.

advanced.overview: Navigating complex figures and marker patterns at canter with balanced speed, self-carriage, and clean lead responses.

components.title: Canter agility and leads
components.description: Balancing through turns and executing planned simple, flying, or counter-canter lines calmly.

advanced.learning: Navigates canter patterns with occasional rushing, wide drifts, or late lead changes.
advanced.proficient: Navigates complex canter figures and marker patterns with balanced speed, responsive alignment, and calm, accurate lead execution.

subject: horse
name: Turn on the Forehand (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to step its hindquarters laterally around a relatively steady forehand in response to light rider requests.
purpose: Builds hindquarter responsiveness and relaxation for gating and lateral work.
safety: Release promptly as the horse steps across to prevent anxiety or backing.

introductory.overview: Stepping the hindquarters calmly through a 90–180° arc around the forehand from halt or slow walk.

components.title: Relaxed hindquarter yield
components.description: Crossing the inside hind leg in front of the outside hind without rushing or backing.

introductory.learning: Yields hindquarters with occasional backward steps, rushing, or bracing against the bit/halter.
introductory.proficient: Calmly steps its hindquarters around the forehand 90–180° in both directions on light requests with minimal drift and relaxed posture.

intermediate.overview: Clean, rhythmic 180–360° turns on the forehand with minimal forehand drift and smooth walk exits.

components.title: Stepping rhythm and straightness
components.description: Maintaining four-beat rhythm and stepping straight forward on request.

intermediate.learning: Completes fuller turns with occasional pivot drift or uneven tempo.
intermediate.proficient: Executes rhythmic, relaxed turns on the forehand in both directions with steady forehand placement and immediate forward walk on request.

subject: horse
name: Turn on the Haunches (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to step its forehand smoothly around an arc while the hindquarters remain relatively anchored.
purpose: Develops shoulder responsiveness, balance, and early collection.
safety: Keep the horse stepping forward in walk rather than twisting on a stuck hind leg.

introductory.overview: Turning the forehand calmly around the haunches on a generous arc from walk without backing or spinning.

components.title: Forward walk turn
components.description: Maintaining active four-beat stepping while bringing the shoulders around.

introductory.learning: Turns the forehand around on wide arcs with occasional pauses, backing, or rushing.
introductory.proficient: Calmly steps its forehand around a small arc from walk in both directions without backing, spinning, or bracing.

intermediate.overview: Compact (~1 m) rhythmic turns on the haunches with soft bend and clean straight exits.

components.title: Compact pivot rhythm
components.description: Inside hind stepping up and down cleanly while forelegs cross smoothly.

intermediate.learning: Performs compact turns with intermittent loss of walk rhythm or pivot stability.
intermediate.proficient: Executes smooth, compact (~1 m) turns on the haunches in both directions while maintaining four-beat rhythm, soft bend, and relaxation.

subject: horse
name: Rein Back (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's calm comprehension, developing balance and diagonal coordination, and adaptable responsiveness when stepping backward under saddle—prioritizing physical comfort and composure.
purpose: Builds attentive softness to light under-saddle requests, balanced body coordination, hindquarter weight acceptance, and calm spatial confidence for everyday handling, gates, trails, and transitions.
safety: Introduce under saddle only after the horse halts settled under a rider and steps back calmly in-hand; release pressure immediately on calm tries rather than pulling continuously on the mouth.
Practice on level, non-slip footing with open, clear space behind so the horse feels safe.

Stepping backward requires comfortable flexion of the hocks, stifles, and lumbar spine—if a horse persistently hollows, tosses its head, drags toes, or refuses despite light, clear cues, assess hock/stifle/back comfort, dental wear, and saddle fit rather than escalating force.

introductory.overview: Fundamental understanding: from a settled halt in calm, open space, calmly understanding a light under-saddle request to shift weight back and take unhurried backward steps within comfortable, unbraced posture natural to its build, then settling quietly into halt when released.

components.title: Calm comprehension and willingness
components.description: Shifting weight back softly on a light request rather than panicking, bracing against the mouth, or running backward out of anxiety.

components.title: Quiet settled pause
components.description: Stopping cleanly when cues release instead of backing unexpectedly afterward or lunging forward.

components.title: Comfort awareness
components.description: Offering honest effort within comfortable posture natural to the horse's conformation without forced framing.

introductory.learning: Responds from halt with brief hesitation, crooked hindquarters, raised head or braced back, dragging feet, or uneven stops and forward/backward drift when released.
introductory.proficient: Calmly understands light under-saddle requests from a settled halt on open ground to step smoothly backward unhurriedly within comfortable, unbraced posture natural to its build, and settles quietly into halt on release without panicking, hollowing defensively, or rushing.

intermediate.overview: Developing balance and coordination: stepping backward willingly in rhythmic diagonal two-beat pairs on light requests with comfortable, functional posture suited to the horse's build—showing improving straightness, soft alignment responsiveness, and calm returns to halt or quiet walk.

components.title: Diagonal two-beat coordination
components.description: Moving diagonal front-and-hind pairs evenly and cleanly without dragging toes, pacing laterally, or rushing backward.

components.title: Functional posture and alignment responsiveness
components.description: Staying soft through jaw and back appropriate to the individual horse's conformation without imposing one idealized outline, and answering gentle shoulder or hip straightening requests politely.

components.title: Calm halt and forward exits
components.description: Returning cleanly to settled halt or unhurried walk when requested.

intermediate.learning: Backs on flat lines with intermittent rushing, dragged hooves, stiffening, uneven alignment responses, or choppy exits into halt or walk.
intermediate.proficient: Steps backward willingly in balanced, rhythmic two-beat diagonal pairs on light cues—maintaining comfortable, unbraced posture suited to its build, responding calmly to gentle alignment requests, and returning quietly to halt or walk without rushing, dragging, or bracing.

advanced.overview: Greater adaptability and refinement: maintaining poised, balanced diagonal coordination through varied demands—such as gentle curves, changes in alignment, varied footing or gentle terrain, busier environments, or optional practical contexts—and transitioning smoothly between backing, halt, and appropriate forward movement (such as walk or trot) with composure and comfort.

components.title: Adaptable balance across alignments and settings
components.description: Carrying steady diagonal rhythm, hindquarter engagement, and emotional composure across gentle backing curves, subtle grades, distracting settings, or optional tight spaces suited to the horse's conditioning.

components.title: Smooth calm forward transitions
components.description: Moving willingly from settled halt or walk into backing and stepping smoothly forward again into balanced walk or trot on light cues without hollowing, rushing, or defensive tension.

advanced.learning: Practices varied alignments, gentle curves or terrain, and smooth forward exits with occasional loss of straightness, rushed departures, or mild brace.
advanced.proficient: Consistently backs with poised, balanced diagonal coordination and soft responsiveness across varied alignments, gentle terrain, busier settings, or optional tight spaces, and transitions smoothly between backing, halt, and balanced walk or trot on light cues without defensive tension or loss of comfort.

subject: horse
name: Sidepass (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to step directly sideways in open space or over a ground rail on light rider requests.
purpose: Enables calm, exact positioning at gates and obstacles.
safety: Keep ground poles stable on flat footing and allow the horse time to see the rail.

intermediate.overview: Stepping evenly sideways in both directions in open space and cleanly over a ground rail.

components.title: Even front and hind crossing
components.description: Keeping the body parallel without rushing or dragging hind legs.

intermediate.learning: Sidepasses with occasional forward/backward drift or touching the rail.
intermediate.proficient: Steps calmly and straight sideways in both directions—including cleanly over a ground rail—on light requests without rushing or knocking the pole.

subject: horse
name: Leg Yield (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to move forward and sideways smoothly at walk or trot with steady rhythm and relaxed acceptance.
purpose: Supples the horse laterally and teaches calm responsiveness to lateral leg requests.
safety: Build gradually with short diagonals so the horse stays balanced and confident.

intermediate.overview: Yielding willingly forward and sideways in both directions at walk and trot.

components.title: Even diagonal crossing
components.description: Maintaining rhythm and straightness/slight flexion without falling through the outside shoulder.

intermediate.learning: Leg yields at walk or trot with occasional rushing, trailing haunches, or shoulder drift.
intermediate.proficient: Moves willingly forward and sideways in both directions at walk and trot with steady rhythm, balance, and relaxation.

subject: horse
name: Shoulder-In (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to travel along a straight line with shoulders slightly inward and uniform bend away from the direction of travel.
purpose: Develops hind-leg engagement, carrying power, and lateral suppleness.
safety: Build strength gradually from shallow angles and short segments.

intermediate.overview: Performing a recognizable, relaxed shoulder-fore or shoulder-in at walk in both directions.

components.title: Walk bend and three-track alignment
components.description: Stepping the inside hind toward the center of mass while keeping steady walk rhythm.

intermediate.learning: Holds shoulder-fore or walk shoulder-in for short stretches with occasional loss of bend or angle.
intermediate.proficient: Carries a recognizable, relaxed shoulder-fore or shoulder-in at walk in both directions along a straight line without drifting or losing rhythm. Trot is not required at this level.

advanced.overview: Sustaining balanced, rhythmic shoulder-in at trot along a full long side in both directions.

components.title: Sustained trot engagement
components.description: Maintaining uniform bend, angle, and cadence through entries, full lines, and exits.

advanced.learning: Sustains trot shoulder-in with intermittent loss of impulsion, bend, or track.
advanced.proficient: Sustains a balanced, rhythmic shoulder-in at trot along a full long side in both directions with uniform bend, engaged inside hind, and calm self-carriage.

subject: horse
name: Travers (Haunches-In, Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's ability to travel along a straight line at walk or trot with slight inward bend (in the direction of travel) and hindquarters carried slightly inward.
purpose: Deepens collection, hindquarter carrying strength, and lateral suppleness.
safety: Keep segments brief while developing strength; never force bend.

advanced.overview: Carrying travers cleanly in both directions at walk and trot with true inward bend and steady rhythm.

components.title: Inward bend and haunches control
components.description: Keeping the forehand on the track while stepping the hindquarters smoothly inward.

advanced.learning: Performs travers at walk or trot with intermittent over-bending, dragging hind feet, or forehand drift.
advanced.proficient: Executes travers in both directions at walk and trot with true inward bend, forehand on the track, engaged hindquarters, and steady rhythm.

subject: horse
name: Terrain & Obstacle Negotiation (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's calm confidence when crossing poles, bridges, tarps, water, slopes, and varied terrain under saddle.
purpose: Develops footwork awareness, trust in the rider, and composure across unfamiliar footing.
safety: Allow the horse to inspect unfamiliar surfaces calmly without forcing or rushing.

introductory.overview: Walking calmly across straightforward obstacles (ground poles, low bridges, tarps, shallow puddles, gentle slopes).

components.title: Calm walk inspection and crossing
components.description: Stepping willingly without balking, leaping, or rushing.

introductory.learning: Crosses straightforward obstacles at walk after brief hesitation or hurried steps on exit.
introductory.proficient: Steps calmly and willingly across straightforward obstacles, shallow water, and gentle terrain at walk in a steady rhythm.

intermediate.overview: Crossing natural water, uneven terrain/slopes, and appropriate trot pole or safe terrain lines calmly under saddle.

components.title: Sure-footed trot and natural water
components.description: Adjusting stride thoughtfully over poles, banks, and deeper/natural water.

intermediate.learning: Negotiates natural water or trot lines with occasional rushing or tension.
intermediate.proficient: Negotiates varied terrain, natural water crossings, and appropriate trot obstacle lines calmly and sure-footedly.

advanced.overview: Maintaining composure and footwork through complex terrain combinations and appropriate canter lines while responding smoothly to pace changes.

components.title: Adjustable canter and down-transitions
components.description: Cantering safe lines smoothly and slowing willingly before technical obstacles.

advanced.learning: Navigates complex terrain or canter lines with intermittent rushing or late pace adjustments.
advanced.proficient: Navigates complex terrain and appropriate canter lines calmly, remaining attentive and willing to slow down on light request.

subject: horse
name: Object Handling (Under Saddle)
summary: The horse's calm cooperation while the rider opens gates or handles, carries, or moves objects from the saddle.
purpose: Reflects trust, patience, and responsiveness to subtle seat/leg cues when the rider's hands are occupied.
safety: Desensitize gradually to gates, ropes, flags, or poles before combining with movement.

introductory.overview: Standing quietly and walking calmly while the rider reaches for, holds, or places simple objects (or navigates an assisted gate).

components.title: Calmness at halt and walk
components.description: Ignoring harmless object movement beside the shoulder or hip.

introductory.learning: Tolerates simple objects at halt or walk with mild tension or stepping away.
introductory.proficient: Stands quietly and walks calmly while the rider handles, carries, or places simple objects without spooking or rushing.

intermediate.overview: Cooperating smoothly through independent gate opening/closing (at halt/walk) and carrying or placing appropriate objects at trot.

components.title: Gate stillness and trot composure
components.description: Stepping into position, waiting calmly while the latch is worked, and ignoring objects carried at trot.

intermediate.learning: Cooperates with gates or trot objects with intermittent restlessness or leaning.
intermediate.proficient: Stands calmly and repositions smoothly for complete gate passages and remains relaxed while objects are carried or handled at trot where appropriate.

advanced.overview: Remaining steady, straight, and responsive on light seat/leg requests during demanding object interactions at canter where appropriate.

components.title: Canter composure around objects
components.description: Holding straightness and rhythm during garrocha, ring, or rope work without flinching.

advanced.learning: Maintains canter around demanding objects with occasional tension or drift.
advanced.proficient: Remains calm, straight, and responsive to one-handed or leg/seat guidance during demanding object handling, including appropriate canter tasks.
